title: Merge a worktree into a local base branch without GitHub, and detect the forge per project
prompt:
The branch panel's Merge step only knows GitHub pull requests, so a project with no GitHub remote, or with gh signed out, has no way to land a worktree's work. Add a local merge: an agent prompt that commits the worktree's work and merges its branch into the local base branch in the main checkout. Which merge the panel offers depends on a per-project forge check. That check has to stay cheap and shared, because every session of a project asks it, and it must refresh when someone signs in to gh or changes the remote.

src/lib/localMerge.ts exports `localMergePrompt(worktree, branch, base, mainCheckout): string`. The prompt treats paths and branch names as data. Inside commands every one of them is POSIX single-quoted, so spaces, quotes and `$(...)` stay literal. Write git commands as `git -C '<main checkout>' ...`. The prompt must contain the following, worded as given:
- `worktree "<worktree>" on branch "<branch>"` and `local base branch "<base>" in the main checkout "<main>"` (values JSON-quoted).
- Stop and report if either checkout has a "merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert in progress". The main checkout must be clean "including untracked files", and nothing is stashed or discarded. "Commit only the worktree's changes".
- Switching the main checkout to the base is written as `...switch the clean main checkout to the named local base branch with <command>; if the branch is missing...`. The command is `git -C <main> switch --no-guess --no-overwrite-ignore -- <base>`.
- The merge is a sentence on its own line: `Run <command>. If the merge conflicts, first record every conflicted file with <list command>, then run <abort command>. Verify the abort succeeded and list the conflicting files in chat.` The merge command is `git -C <main> merge --no-edit --no-autostash --no-overwrite-ignore -- 'refs/heads/<branch>'`, so a tag with the same name cannot stand in for the branch and ignored local files are never overwritten. The list command is `git -C <main> diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`, and the abort is `git -C <main> merge --abort`.
- "Do not resolve conflicts, retry the merge, reset, or discard changes". Report an abort failure. After success, verify that the worktree HEAD is an ancestor of the base. "report the main checkout's final branch". No push and no pull request. "Leave the worktree and branch in place".

src/lib/projectForge.ts exports `projectForge(path): Promise<ProjectForge>` and `useProjectForge(path: string | null): ProjectForge | undefined`, using `api.projectForge(cwd)` (`invoke("project_forge", { cwd })`, type `"github" | "githubUnavailable" | "localOnly"`, with the Rust command in github.rs/branch_overview.rs):
- One check per path is shared by every caller while it is in flight, however long it takes. After it completes, the answer is kept for 60 s, or for 10 s when it is `"githubUnavailable"`, counted from completion. A rejected check counts as `"githubUnavailable"`.
- The hook rechecks whenever the document becomes visible (a `visibilitychange` event while not hidden) and every 60 s. For a new path it returns undefined until that path's own answer arrives; it never shows the previous project's forge.

Then use these in the branch panel (src/components/changes/BranchPanel.tsx, NextStep.tsx) and TabView: offer the local merge for local-only projects or when GitHub is unavailable. Telling a local forge apart from GitHub must not depend on gh being authenticated, and the check must not disturb GitHub workflows.

check.run: pnpm exec vitest run src/lib/localMerge.test.ts src/lib/projectForge.test.tsx

notes:
Source: PR #827, four commits.
Chain: 7ce042cb introduces src/lib/localMerge.ts and src/lib/projectForge.ts, with the Rust forge check in branch_overview.rs/github.rs and their use in BranchPanel.tsx and TabView.tsx. 5092be58 changes both new modules (localMerge.ts and projectForge.ts) and the same Rust and panel files, so that GitHub workflows survive forge checks. e46e6755 changes projectForge.ts and github.rs again, to detect local forges without gh authentication. 005abf94 fixes the WebKit checks broken by the header and menu changes in SessionView.tsx.
Later commits edit the modules and functions the first one created.
The check is the PR's two new unit tests. localMerge.test.ts runs the prompt's commands against real temporary git repositories. BranchPanel/TabView UI tests are left out because main changed them inside the PR.
